title: Constantinople: Maxim's Cabaret and Mr. Thomas
summary: A German booking office sent Briggs to a Constantinople cabaret run by Mr. Thomas of Savannah, who had fled Russia; it was shut by police and the band was poorly fed.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: From Vienna, we went to Constantinople, Turkey.
What was that? Was that 'a dance band, was it?
No, -- a dance band, yes. I had an engagement through the booking
Briggs
office, German booking office, for Constantinople.
What was that like?
The Cabaret. Maxim's Cabaret.
Right.
It was run by a black man, who was one of these Russian refugees to Turkey. His name was Mr. Thomas.
Thomas?
Thomas. He was from Savannah, Georgia.
But how had he been in Russia?
You see, he had been in Russia for quite some time, because he left Russia with what you call the Russian aristocrats.
I was told that he had had a cabaret in Russia.
I see, what was his first name?
Briggs
I don't remember.
His last name was Thomas.
Thomas from Savannah, Georgia.
And he had been in Russia, I suppose for some time.

Yes, yes, he'd managed to get to Turkey. And he opened this cabaret. But the thing that we didn't know is his financial situation wasn't so good. We opened in Turkey, and formed it within a month, and went to work one evening and there was a notice on the door that the club was closed by the police, by the government.
Because he was just out of money?
Out of money. He had many debts, and everything else, and as a matter of fact, he -- we had a pretty rough few time, we tried to get the/francs that he owed
Briggs 152
us.
Right, right.

So we had notice that we had a contract where we'd get our dinner in the evening, and we realized that -- in two or three days we'd stopped eating the food that they served us, because two or three of us got ill, we felt.
Right.
We had stomach trouble and everything else. And we realized that he was doing everything to save money.
I see.
